solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Childless female's energy field

parts.note: s.p. is the genealogists' abbreviation for sine prole, Latin for 'without issue'
her is the female possessive pronoun
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A woman without children has a certain energy field around her.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole, 'without children') is a family-tree abbreviation many solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of activity or influence is a sphere, as in 'her sphere of expertise'.

clue.text: Threat at sea aboard wrecks

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: aboard means on a ship, and SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A threat at sea brings down the vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter means 'aboard' as 'in SS': the rearranged THREAT, HATTER, sits inside the steamship's S and S. Shuffling all eight letters together lands in the same place.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck something is to smash it to pieces, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Felicity longs to get into shape, endlessly cycling around

indicators.note: to get into means the yearning word is placed inside the other
cycling around means the first letter of the shortened word is carried to its end
endlessly means the final letter of the word shape is dropped

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: A woman called Felicity longs to get fit by cycling everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last E; 'cycling around' moves the front S to the back, giving HAPS, split by 'to get into'.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is a formal word for great contentment or joy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spots the Queen making something to eat

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: The Queen breaks out in spots while preparing a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of bacon is food, so 'something to eat' describes it loosely.

clue.text: Co-ordinate muscles like so, when retiring

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the two short words are read in reverse

parts.note: as means like, in 'as a child'
sic is Latin for 'so', used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: Muscles coordinate like so when a person withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns AS + SIC into CISSA; 'when' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: On a graph, the horizontal x-value of a point is one of its two coordinates.

clue.text: French letter possibly split in gateway

parts.note: 'gateway' split in two gives gate, and a gate is a barrier
the second half of the split word is way, and a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A condom might split at the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split in gateway' tells you to break the word into gate and way, then take a synonym of each. 'French letter' is British slang for a condom.
explanation.definitionFit: Condoms block sperm physically, an example of this class of contraception, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Tom's hand tool

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so tom's gives the cat's
a paw is an animal's hand, or slangily a human one

explanation.surface: Tom owns a hand tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand tool' reads as one phrase, but 'hand' gives PAW and 'tool' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person used by another to do dirty work is a pawn or dupe, from the fable of the monkey using a cat's paw to grab chestnuts.

clue.text: Dance with male graduate

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: Someone dances with a man who has just graduated.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian ballroom and carnival style, so an example of a dance.

clue.text: A girl turns up on second property

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl appears on a second property.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessions of value held by a person or firm are its holdings, a synonym for property.

clue.text: Nice here in quarters near the sea, surrounded by mountains

indicators.note: surrounded by means the mountain range is split to hold the other pieces

parts.note: the Alps are a mountain range
E and S are two compass quarters, east and south
maritime means bordering on or near the sea

explanation.surface: Nice is here, in districts by the coast with mountains all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French Riviera city, not the adjective; the range's last letter is parted from the rest by 'surrounded by'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French département on the Riviera whose capital is the city of Nice.

clue.text: See 9
Bovine complaint contracted in absentia

parts.note: a cattle illness, whose shortened form, the initials of bovine spongiform encephalopathy, sits inside the word absentia

explanation.surface: A cow catches an illness while away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' means shortened: the disease's initials BSE sit in 'aBSEntia'; the clue points to the disease but no wordplay builds the full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The popular name for bovine spongiform encephalopathy, a brain illness of cattle.

clue.text: Last part of dental treatment: one filling

indicators.note: filling means the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
treatment means the word dental is processed and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The last part of dental work is putting in one filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' turns DENTAL into TALEND; 'filling' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The final section or end of something, such as the tail end of a queue.

clue.text: Setter's to arrange time for false tooth?

parts.note: the setter is 'I', and setter's is I'm, short for I am
to plan something is to arrange it

explanation.surface: The setter has to fix a time for fitting a false tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental implant is an artificial tooth anchored into the jaw; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Basket of fish not caught by one holding fishing line

indicators.note: not means the caught letter is left out of the basket word

parts.note: a creel is an angler's wicker basket for fish
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An angler's basket doesn't catch the fish held on the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The winding device on a rod stores the angler's line, so it holds fishing line.

clue.text: Library user, maybe one claiming iPod found under floorboards?

definitions.meaning: someone who takes books out on loan

definitions.text: one claiming iPod found under floorboards?
definitions.meaning: Mary Norton's children's books The ... are about tiny people living under the floorboards who take small things from humans

explanation.walkthrough: The Borrowers is a classic British children's book; its little people 'borrow' items, so one might claim a lost iPod.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes items on loan, whether a library member or one of Norton's little people.

clue.text: Working out what's due as punishment

definitions.meaning: retribution, as in a day of judgement for wrongdoing

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a calculation and a settling of accounts for one's wrongdoing.

clue.text: Leather does, perhaps?

parts.note: female deer are relatives of the male deer, so they could be called the male deer's family

explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is not the verb but female deer, read as 'buck's kin'; 'Leather' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft leather made from deer or sheep hide, the hide of a male deer originally.

clue.text: Starts to seek hiding-place, looking more embarrassed? This might destroy the evidence

indicators.note: starts to means only the first letters of seek and hiding-place are used

parts.note: someone more embarrassed goes redder in the face

explanation.surface: A guilty person blushes and looks for somewhere to hide the evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that cuts documents into strips is used to get rid of incriminating papers.

clue.text: Eating pork pie, always brought up discharge

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other
brought up in a down clue means the word is read upward, i.e. reversed

parts.note: ever means always
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie

explanation.surface: Someone eating pork pie keeps bringing it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' is rhyming slang for lie (a pork pie is a British meat pie). 'brought up' gives REVE, which 'Eating' wraps round the fib.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge someone from a duty or post is to relieve them of it.

clue.text: Colour of the crustaceans

indicators.note: of here means the letters are taken from within the words the crustaceans

explanation.surface: A question about the colour of shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale greyish-yellow shade, like unbleached linen.

clue.text: Small person going round with jerk

indicators.note: going round means the small person surrounds the other letter

parts.note: a titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A little person goes round with an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an insult for the small person, but it is a sudden spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden involuntary movement or spasm is a jerk.

clue.text: Very drunk before starting game

indicators.note: starting means only the first letter of before is used

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: Someone gets very drunk before a game begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for extremely intoxicated, a synonym of plastered.

clue.text: Rabbits on edges of fields facing country houses

indicators.note: houses means the country holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Wales is a country of the UK
the leading edges, or starting letters, of the words fields and facing

explanation.surface: Rabbits sit on the edges of fields in front of country houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbits on' is British for talks at length, not animals; 'houses' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle without substance, a British idiom for chattering.

clue.text: Sally Field's first love, a swimmer

indicators.note: Field's first means the first letter of the word Field's

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Sally Field's first love was a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally Field is an American actress; 'Sally' is the definition, a sudden military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden excursion or raid, a synonym.

clue.text: Drinking bad wine in Barrow?

indicators.note: drinking means the wine takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: hock is a German white wine
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Someone drinking bad wine in the town of Barrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow looks like Barrow-in-Furness, an English town, but a barrow is an ancient burial mound.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is an earth mound; a small mound is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Find the lady playing cricket, rather entertaining daughter

indicators.note: entertaining means the word rather holds the daughter letter
playing means the letters are being played about with

explanation.surface: Playing cricket while entertaining a daughter, someone tries to find a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find the lady' names a card con, not an instruction. 'playing' makes THREECARTRICK of the two words; 'entertaining' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Find the lady is another name for the street con with three cards in which the punter must spot the queen.

clue.text: See 25
Play with passion on grass

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after the grass word

parts.note: hay is dried grass
fever is passion or excitement

explanation.surface: Acting with passion on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is Noël Coward's 1925 comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Noël Coward's comedy about the eccentric Bliss family.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink knocked back by working woman that's monstrously repulsive

indicators.note: knocked back means the drink is reversed, as well as gulped

parts.note: grog is rum diluted with water
on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A working woman downs a drink and becomes monstrously ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses GROG into GORG.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, Medusa and her sisters were monstrous women whose gaze turned people to stone.
